{{nihongo|'''Takahashi Shrine'''|高橋神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Takahashi Shrine''' (たかはしじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Hachijō, {{ill|Nara (city)|Q169134|qid=Q169134}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} with former rank {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Two deities are enshrined, both regarded as founder deities of cuisine and clan deities of the Takahashi no Omi:
:{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto}} (イワカムツカリノミコト)
:{{ill|Takuhadachiji-hime|de|Yorozuhatahime|ja|栲幡千千姫命|ru|Ёродзухататоёакицуси-химэ-но микото|zh|栲幡千千姬命|qid=Q11110848}} (タチハタチヂヒメノミコト)

=== History ===
The origin of Takahashi Shrine is unclear, but it appears certain that a place name "Takahashi" existed in this area in antiquity.

In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, an epidemic spread and many people died. The emperor, grieving, saw {{ill|Ōmononushi|fr|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|mni|ꯑꯣꯃꯣꯅꯣꯅꯨꯁꯤ|ru|Омононуси|simple|Ōmononushi|zh|大物主|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Kami}} in a dream saying, "This epidemic is my will. If Ōtataneko worships me, the curse will disappear and the country will be at peace." The emperor then found Ōtataneko and had him worship Ōmononushi as priest, and the epidemic ceased as foretold. In this ritual, a person named Ikuto from Takahashi village in Soekami District, Yamato, was appointed as sake-offering attendant to present sacred sake.

Also, according to the entry for {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}} year 53 in the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}},' when Keikō toured the east and reached {{ill|Kazusa Province|Q1055394|qid=Q1055394}}, he obtained a white clam while crossing a sea route. The attendant deity prepared it as namasu and offered it, and the emperor greatly praised its taste, granting him the title of Kashiwade no Omi. Ten generations later, the title Takahashi no Ason was additionally granted. The ancestor of this Takahashi no Ason (Kashiwade no Omi) was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto}}, and descendants hereditary-held Naizen duties for imperial meals; later they came to be worshiped as deity of cuisine. The change of surname from Kashiwade to Takahashi is thought related to this place name.

The former site was about 100 m north of the current location, but is said to have burned in warfare by {{ill|Matsunaga Hisahide|cs|Hisahide Macunaga|de|Matsunaga Hisahide|fa|ماتسوناگا هیساهیده|fr|Matsunaga Hisahide|it|Matsunaga Hisahide|ja|松永久秀|ko|마쓰나가 히사히데|ru|Мацунага Хисахидэ|sk|Hisahide Macunaga|sr|Мацунага Хисахиде|uk|Мацунаґа Хісахіде|zh|松永久秀|qid=Q1143038}} in the {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} era and moved to the present site. Later, three sacred mirrors were unearthed at the old site and are enshrined as shrine treasures.

=== Rites ===
[[File:高橋神社 月次祭.jpg|150px|thumb|Takahashi Shrine monthly rite]]
=== Hōtō-shiki ===
Every May, wishing prosperity of people bearing the Takahashi surname nationwide and advancement in culinary skills, the shrine performs "Hōtō-shiki," demonstrating the classical knife tradition {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōkusa-ryū Hōchōdō}}<ref name="産経ニュース">[https://www.sankei.com/article/20170515-SNG6BXYEIVOGBIHPANADTLZJRM/ "Hōtō-shiki" at Nara Takahashi Shrine; chief priest demonstrates elegant handling - Sankei News] viewed April 9, 2018</ref>. The rite existed from old times but had lapsed; from 2015 it was revived as a shrine ceremony<ref name="産経ニュース" />.
